t: You're standing on the Bazalgette Embankment, on the north bank of the Thames in the City of London. It is new, created in 2025, and it is the first embankment made in London in 150 years. It is 250 metres long, and it is one of seven planned embankments created by building the Thames Tideway Tunnel. The architects were Fereday Pollard and Hawkins Brown. It is named for Joseph Bazalgette, the engineer who built central London's main drainage after the Great Stink of 1858, helping to end the cholera epidemics and begin cleaning the river.
